transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I'm going through a foreclosure right now. And I know how that sounds—I really don't want to come across as difficult or, you know, unreasonable. Is it okay if I just explain what's been happening? 

Everyone keeps acting like this is just a normal situation, just standard paperwork and missed payments. But... I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and honestly even some of the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing the signs of it for almost two years now, and... well, no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing happen behind the scenes. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering your question properly.
During this time, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing like that. I hope it's okay to say, but I definitely haven't heard any voices or sounds that aren't there. I know sometimes stress can make people, you know, imagine things, but for me it's really just... just noticing the things they are actually doing, the real things. Does that make sense? Am I answering that right?
Over the past several months, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or unable to enjoy things?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, obviously dealing with the house situation is stressful, but... I wouldn't say I'm depressed at all. I still really like going to work—I manage a retail team, so I like to keep a good face on for them anyway—and I still enjoy my regular routine. 

I try really hard to keep a positive attitude through all of this, you know? I hope that's okay to say... I just don't want to sound like I'm complaining or wallowing or anything. But no, I definitely haven't been feeling persistently down. Is it okay that my mood has been mostly fine? Am I making sense?
Looking back over your life, even before this house situation started, have you generally found it hard to trust people or felt that people around you had hidden motives?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I've always been a really trusting person, honestly. I mean, working in retail management, you kind of have to be a people person, right? I've always gotten along great with my friends and my staff. 

Before all this started with the bank... I never really second-guessed anyone's motives. I always try to see the best in people. I hope that doesn't make me sound naive or anything? It's just... this specific situation with the house is so different because of what they're actually doing. But normally, in my regular life, no, I trust people just fine. 

Is it okay that I say that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I usually am.
